title: A directory on a disk
question: The same mkdir, on ext4: what does a directory look like on a disk?
text: The same mkdir as in memory, but on ext4. What does a directory look like on a disk?

1. [ext4_mkdir](1:ext4_mkdir) makes the directory in one journal transaction. On a disk a directory is a file of names, so [ext4_init_new_dir](1:ext4_init_new_dir) writes its first block with its own two entries, "." (itself) and ".." (its parent), and [ext4_add_entry](1:ext4_add_entry) puts the name "sub" into a block of /mnt, the parent.
2. Listing /mnt: [ext4_readdir](3:ext4_readdir) reads the directory's blocks and hands out one entry after another.
Try: [list the new directory instead](try:1): only "." and "..". Or make a file in it first, then list it.
tries: char buf[256]; mkdirat(AT_FDCWD, "/mnt/sub", 0755); fd = openat(AT_FDCWD, "/mnt/sub", O_RDONLY | O_DIRECTORY); getdents64(fd, buf, 256); close(fd)
